newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures close mostly lower.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures close mostly lower.

text.p: March 17 - IMM currency futures closed mostly lower in light pit trade. Marks remained slightly higher, while most Swiss franc contracts held a weak tone. Traders said growing speculation that the U.S. Fed will hike rates next week added little pressure to the range-bound key currencies.
Traders and analysts said June marks could fall to $0.5908 or 1.7025 dollar/mark if the Fed hikes short-term rates a quarter basis point, but most do not anticipate a "runaway rally" in the dollar.
One analyst said dollar/mark could dip to 1.6675 in the interim, which would mean a rise to $0.6030 in June marks.
Between now and March 25, they said the currency futures markets would be driven more by the cash mark than the dollar.
"The pivotal thing is the mark, not the dollar," said John Nelson, senior vice president and forex manager at ABN AMRO Bank in Chicago.
He said demand for marks against most currencies, including sterling and yen, put medium-term dollar positions in jeopardy.
June sterling fell to $1.5828, holding above key support at $1.5820, while June yen held losses fractionally above support at $0.008182 or 123.80 spot.
Meanwhile, June marks traded above resistance at $0.5931 and $0.5959, which corresponded to two support levels the dollar breached at 1.6960 and 1.6880, Nelson said.
Further resistance is at $0.5976 or about 1.6830 spot marks.
Traders said mark strength on the cash crosses was based on German finance minister Theo Waigel's comments.
Waigel was quoted in Bild, a German daily newspaper, as saying that fulfilling the criteria for European Monetary Union was more important than sticking to a strict timetable.

"There is a lot of apprehension and interest about EMU news," one trader said. "If EMU looks like it will go without a glitch, that's dollar positive. If it looks like there will be millions of problems, that's beneficial for the mark."

At the end of pit trade, June yen was off $0.000019 at $0.008192, marks were up $0.0011 at $0.5949, Swiss francs were off $0.0017 at $0.6913, sterling was off $0.0132 at $1.5856, Canadian dollars were down $0.0028 at $0.7342, Australian dollars were $0.0047 lower at $0.7921 and Mexican pesos were $0.000225 higher at $0.120375.
